summary: Nora carries her own account of what she is in the file that already says who she is, instead of fetching it mid-question. Nothing she says about herself changes; when she has it does.
details: The self-account shipped on 2026-09-13 as a loadable skill. A skill only reaches her if the model spends one of two budgeted calls going to get it — and the moment it is needed is somebody in a room asking her what she is, which is the worst moment to expect her to stop and look herself up. It now sits in the doctrine file that already carries who she is and where she comes from, in front of her on every path that reads that file.
The words are unchanged. Every sentence was reviewed when it shipped and every claim in it is still pinned by the same tests, which now read it where it lives.

Two things it gains by being doctrine rather than a skill. Its place in the ordering that says which instruction wins when two disagree is now real — on a skill those lines were written down and nothing read them. And the check that stops her reciting her own instructions back to a room now covers it; a skill body was outside that check and is served over the web besides.
limitations: Whether this changes what she actually says under pressure is not established here. The corpus that would answer it could not see the skill at all — it runs her doctrine with no skills loaded — so the first reading taken of it, hours before this change, measured her without the account. That reading is now possible for the first time and is the thing that closes the issue behind this.

The account describes the shape of what she is and names no instance of anything — no page, no version, no address. That is deliberate: this same file carried a list of what she could do for eight weeks after it stopped being true, and an instance is the part that goes stale in silence.
